web_evidence.title: Tinker Tailor Soldier Spy — Penguin Classics sample
web_evidence.note: The authorized 41-page publisher sample sustains third-person narration across the opening chapters and shifts focalization among Roach, Prideaux, Smiley, and Guillam without introducing a participating narrator.

web_evidence.title: Margaret Atwood Recommends 12 Examples of Point of View in Literature
web_evidence.note: MasterClass places the novel in Atwood's third-person reading list and explicitly characterizes it as third-person narration shaped by the many-character novel.

web_evidence.title: John le Carré Writing Styles in Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Spy
web_evidence.note: The study guide explicitly states that the book is written in third person and explains that Smiley is the principal focal character while events beyond his presence are also narrated.

web_evidence.title: Undercover: Le Carre Trips on His Own Tricks (Rolling Stone, 1980)
web_evidence.note: The criticism describes le Carré's relevant novels as using an anonymous third person generally focalized through Smiley and specifically identifies Smiley's central role in Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Spy.

person_note: The controlling narrator is nonparticipating and third person. Numerous interior quote passages sustain external narration while moving through the perceptions of Smiley, Guillam, Prideaux, Jackie Lacon, Mendel, and others; this agrees with the authorized Penguin opening and explicit whole-book POV descriptions. Visible first-person forms belong to dialogue, autobiographical anecdotes, or directly represented thoughts, while second-person forms are dialogue, instruction, or generic address. Generic inclusive 'we' passages do not make the narrator a story participant. The novel shifts focal character and contains embedded recollections and documents, but the research found no sustained base section in another grammatical person. The main scope limitation is that the Tier A publisher evidence covers the opening rather than the entire novel, offset by extensive interior quotations and multiple explicit whole-book descriptions.
